To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the regional health-care systems are very vulnerable, in particular to the loss of beds and operating rooms, that the most vulnerable hospitals in terms of the loss of beds are the ones with a high number of beds and the ones located in areas of higher seismic hazard and that the most vulnerable in terms of the reduction of the operating room capacity are the ones with more operating rooms and with a high number and high percentage of beds in the operating rooms.

the proposed probabilistic model for the seismic vulnerability of health-care systems is a valuable tool to estimate the impact and to quantify the capability of a regional health care system to cope with the increased demand of medical care that follows a seismic event, and that the model can be used to identify the most vulnerable components of the health-care system and the most critical areas in terms of the capability to provide medical care after an earthquake.

the regional health-care systems are able to cope with the medical care demand in most cases and that a significant increase in the number of casualties is observed only in the case of a very large earthquake.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) the definition of the seismic demand for the regional health-care systems; (ii) the estimation of the number of operating theatres and beds available in the hospitals hit by a seismic hazard; (iii) the assessment of the capability of the regional health-care network to cope with the medical demand arising from a seismic hazard; and (iv) the definition of a probabilistic methodology for the seismic risk analysis of the health-care systems at the regional scale.

the development and application of a probabilistic model for the seismic vulnerability of a regional health system, with the aim to provide a tool to assess the impact of an extreme event on the regional health system and to evaluate the capability of the system to cope with the resulting medical demand.

the following questions: how to assess the impact of an event on a health-care system; what is the probability that the system is unable to cope with the post-earthquake demand for medical care, as a function of the magnitude of the seismic event; what is the expected number of patients that cannot be treated in the hospital facilities of the system; how to identify the most critical elements of the infrastructure, in terms of their contribution to the vulnerability of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although it is difficult to quantify the exact impact on the regional health care system of an earthquake in the region, the results presented here indicate that a significant number of hospitals would not function at full capacity and that the number of available beds would be reduced.

the seismic assessment of health care systems, as a part of a more complex and integrated assessment framework, is feasible and that it can contribute to the improvement of the resilience and the sustainability of the health care systems.

the seismic vulnerability assessment model developed in this work can be used to provide useful information for emergency planning, to identify and prioritize retrofitting interventions, to estimate the economic impact of a seismic event and to evaluate the capability of a regional health care system to cope with the post-earthquake demand of medical care, by taking into account both the physical and functional vulnerability of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a model for the seismic vulnerability of health-care systems, which is based on a probabilistic approach and is able to provide a quantitative measure of the impact of an event on the health-care system and on the population, in the form of a probabilistic distribution of the number of casualties.

the paper proposes a methodology for the probabilistic evaluation of the impact of an seismic event on a health-care system, in terms of its capability to cope, in the post-disaster phase, with the demand of health care arising from the earthquake, and the capability of a road network to support the evacuation of patients.

the paper presents an approach for the seismic vulnerability and performance assessment of health-care facilities and their interconnection with other infrastructural systems, and it is applied to a case study of a health-care system and its interconnection with a road network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a seismic event may have a severe impact not only on hospitals but also on the entire health-care system.

the regional health-care systems in the study area can provide a satisfactory level of medical care to the population, even under the most adverse conditions, such as the occurrence of a large earthquake and a high level of damage to the hospitals.

, in the presence of interconnections between the health-care and road systems, a seismic hazard scenario that does not affect all roads in a region is not sufficient for a correct assessment of the health-care system performance.
